title: Ancient feeding-related neuropeptides regulate alloparenting in ants.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the whole GitHub repo tree (82 entries) and read its README plus one AntMaxDistance CSV. The repo holds one demo experiment of 24 young ants (AnTrax tracking .mat files, per-ant distance CSVs, 4 notebooks); the README says this experiment 'is not published in Paul et al. 2026'. Europe PMC supplementary-file endpoint timed out after 75 s, so the per-figure source data tables were not opened.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Sample sizes from figure legends: 61 synthesized neuropeptides screened at n = 12 ants each; the largest single comparison is 143 young versus 143 old ants; other panels use 7 to 90 per group. Data availability says all data are in the Supplementary Information and Source Data files.

a1_downloadable.note: The GitHub demo data downloads freely; the Nature source data is said to be open but I could not retrieve it (supplement endpoint timed out).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not decisive: behaviour summaries (time in contact with larva, phase 1 duration) are computed per ant by the authors' notebooks, so they would be per-ant columns in source data; not verified in files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Neuropeptide sequences (7–35 amino acids) are described in the paper; not checked in files.

a4_units_stated.note: Proportions of time and durations in the paper legends; not checked in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Fails. The only peptide-level task has 61 peptides (12 ants each, per paper text); the largest per-ant comparison is 143 + 143 ants with a two-level age label. Far below ~400 labelled rows for any meaningful prediction task.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The only data I could open (24-ant demo) is explicitly not part of the published experiments, so no published count could be checked against files.

a8_label_provenance.note: Behaviour labels come from automated video tracking (AnTrax) of real ants, i.e. a measurement, though contact scores are derived from tracked positions.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) could embed the 61 peptides, but n is far too small

honest_claim_h3: Any model would be fitting 61 peptide effects measured in one ant species by one lab, which supports no generalisable claim.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a neuropeptide's amino-acid sequence to predict whether it raises or lowers brood-care behaviour in ants.
plain_idea.train_on: Each of 61 synthesized clonal raider ant neuropeptides (sequence), with the average behaviour of 12 treated ants per peptide (from paper text; files not opened).
plain_idea.predict: Change in time young ants spend touching a larva after peptide treatment, measured by automated video tracking.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would flag candidate behaviour-modulating peptides in other social insects, but 61 examples from one species cannot support that.

ml_idea: Peptide sequence to behavioural effect regression, or per-ant age classification from tracking features; both too small (61 peptides; 286 ants with a binary label).

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes in the repo listing; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count peptides in the screen (61, per paper) — already kills it.

verdict_reason: Fails A5: a lab behavioural study with 61 screened peptides and at most 143 ants per group; the only openable data is a 24-ant demo the README says is not in the paper, so A7 cannot be checked either.
